question: Can a parameter-free selector using only the eight deployment-visible frames choose among the solve-free anchor and two frozen B2 corrections well enough to improve unseen future frames?
hypothesis: Observed-prefix relative L2 ranks whether a frozen correction is trustworthy on the same record, so choosing the lowest-prefix-error option will improve future relative L2 without reading future truth.
literature_and_project_basis: The acoustic research map ranks observation-conditioned correction with calibrated abstention as a low-cost route, and prior project R49/R50 evidence showed that abstention can protect nonworse behavior. This probe uses an analytic argmin and no fitted threshold.

mechanism.selection_metric: relative L2 on frames 0 through 7 only
mechanism.selection_rule: per record, choose the option with minimum observed-prefix relative L2; deterministic first-option tie break
mechanism.future_truth_use: after the option index is fixed, score frames 8 through 63

gate.primary_metric: selected future relative L2 over frames 8 through 63, averaged over 30 records
gate.family_gate: selected future mean must be strictly below anchor for uniform, layered, and marmousi
gate.failure_signal: reject the current B2 development-fit plus causal-abstention route if any aggregate, nonworse, or family subgate fails

budget.runtime_caveat: two B2 corrections are evaluated, so this probe makes no 10x deployment-runtime claim

rollback: additive diagnostic only; preserve all source checkpoints and protected families; retain any failed terminal/log and never reuse a partial cache
claim_scope: A pass supports only prefix-observation-conditioned selection on fresh train records. It does not promote B2, count as complete validation/test_id evidence, or satisfy runtime requirements. A fail rejects this rescue route and requires any future B2 work to begin with train-only fit/calibration/confirmation rather than the 90-record development-fit checkpoints.
